title: Two riders, one nearest driver
description: Two matching workers handle riders a block apart. Both query the geo index and both pick driver d_7 as closest. Occasionally d_7 ends up assigned to both rides. Which fix gives one-driver-one-ride while keeping matching fast?

options.text: Refresh the geo index more often so workers see d_7's status change sooner
options.explanation: Fresher reads narrow the race window but never close it; two workers can still read 'available' at the same instant.

options.text: Reserve d_7 with a short-lived lease (SET NX with a TTL) before offering, and assign on accept with conditional writes that require the ride to be matching and the driver to be available or offered for this ride
options.explanation: The lease stops duplicate offers cheaply; the conditional writes are the correctness boundary, so even an expired lease or late accept cannot double-assign.

options.text: Route all matching for the whole country through a single worker
options.explanation: Serialisation removes the race but creates a throughput bottleneck and a single point of failure for every city.

options.text: Use a distributed lock with a 10-minute TTL and assign the driver when the lock is acquired
options.explanation: A long lock leaves the driver unusable when offers are ignored, and with no conditional write behind it, an expired or lost lock can still lead to double assignment.
